sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed for following reliefs:
i) Issue writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ or order or quashing award notice dated 22.08.2023 issued by respondent no.2 in no.CKM-SKP/06/2018-19 as per Annexure-H.
ii) Issue writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order or directing respondent in name of petitioner herein and by treating entire land in Sy.no.20/26,
to extent of 07 guntas situated at Gotravalli village, Kasba Hobli, Belur Taluk, Hassan District, as converted land and pay compensation as per market value with all statutory benefits etc.
2. Sri Vigneshwar S Shastri, learned Senior Counsel appearing for Sri Sagar V Shastri, advocate for petitioner submitted that petitioner was original owner of land bearing Sy.no.20/26, to extent of 07 guntas situated at Gotravalli village, Kasba Hobli, Belur Taluk, Hassan District under registered sale deed dated 02.01.2014.
After purchase, petitioner applied for its conversion in respect of 25 guntas for non-agricultural purpose.
Same was granted by Deputy Commissioner, Hassan by order dated 15.10.2018.

In meanwhile, respondent no.2 had initiated acquisition NC: 2023:KHC:39658 proceedings against petitioner's land to an extent of 07 guntas and award notice dated 06.09.2019 was issued under provisions of Section 21(1)(2) of Right to Fair Compensation, and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re- Settlement Act, 2013, for purpose of Chikkamagalur- Sakaleshpur New Broad-gauge Railway Development Plan.

sentences.text: 3. It was further submitted that, respondent no.2 had considered acquired land as agricultural land while issuing impugned award notice at Annexure-H.

And that under similar circumstances,
co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.no.19545/2022 disposed of on 28.08.2023 had directed respondents to re-consider representations in accordance with law.

4. On other hand, Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned counsel for respondents submitted that assessment of compensation was made taking same as agricultural land since petitioner had merely stated that acquired land was converted, without producing order of conversion and same may have lapsed.
Therefore, sought for dismissal of writ petition.

5. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.

sentences.text: From above submission, it is seen that though petitioner's has land was converted for non-agricultural purposes under Official Memorandum issued by Deputy Commissioner, on 15.10.2018 at Annexure-B, SLAO failed to consider same while issuing impugned award notice.
Further, there is no provision in Karnataka Land Revenue Act, which would terminate order of conversion merely due to non- compliance with any conditions imposed in conversion order.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that impugned notice issued by respondent no.2-SLAO cannot be sustained.
Consequently, Writ Petition is allowed.
Impugned notice dated 22.08.2023 issued by respondent no.2 in no.CKM- SKP/06/2018-19 as per Annexure-H is quashed.

Respondent no.2 is directed to consider representations dated 11.09.2023 at Annexure -J and J1 and pass appropriate orders thereon in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible within an outer limit of two months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
